summary: Mostly a type-level refactor of the @cipherstash/stack encryption client: the `as never` forwarding casts in createEncryptionClient are replaced by real signatures (PlaintextInput, EncryptQueryArgs, BulkEncryptPayloadInput), and FFI plaintext casts are centralised in an identity helper `toJsPlaintext`. Runtime behaviour of encrypt/encryptQuery/bulkEncrypt/model paths is unchanged on read: the native encryptQuery branches on args[1] exactly as it branched on `opts`, and no payload shape changes. Two contract changes ship: (1) `encrypt` on a `types.Json` column whose plaintext type admits null now returns `data: Encrypted | null`, which will stop some consumers' code compiling, released as a minor bump; (2) the stack-supabase per-term fallback now fails closed on a null envelope instead of sending the string "null" as a filter operand. No silent data, key or plaintext-exposure mechanism was found. Tests (type tests, forwarding unit tests, supabase fallback test, a JSON null-element integration test) were added but not run here and no CI was supplied.

behaviour_changes.description:
EncryptionClient.encrypt is generic over the plaintext type P and returns EncryptOperation>, where EncryptResult

= Encrypted | (null & P). For a types.Json column with a literal null or a JsonDocument-typed value, the success data type widens from Encrypted to Encrypted | null (also through withLockContext/audit). Runtime value unchanged: null plaintext already resolved to { data: null }.

Exported operation classes EncryptOperation / EncryptOperationWithLockContext gain an optional result type parameter R (default Encrypted); EncryptOperation, EncryptQueryOperation, BatchEncryptQueryOperation and BulkEncryptOperation accept PlaintextInput (adds JsonDocument) and their getOperation() return types widen. EncryptResult is newly exported from @cipherstash/stack/encryption.

Typed client's encryptQuery now forwards its caller's arguments verbatim with ...args to the native encryptQuery, which discriminates single vs batch on args[1] instead of a named opts parameter. Batch calls now reach the native method with exactly one argument rather than (terms, undefined). Routing logic is equivalent on read.

stack-supabase encryptGroupPerTerm (fallback used only when the client has no bulkEncrypt) now raises an encryption failure on a null envelope instead of JSON.stringify-ing it to "null" and sending it as a filter operand, matching the bulk path.

FFI plaintext casts (`as JsPlaintext`) replaced by an identity helper toJsPlaintext; internal NativeEncryptionClient.encryptModel/bulkEncryptModels lose their schema-aware generics (now Record<string, unknown>), with the typed client re-asserting V3EncryptedModel. NativeEncryptionClient is not exported; Encryption() always wraps it with createEncryptionClient.
The shipped stash-encryption agent skill now documents that encrypt on a types.Json column resolves null to { data: null } typed Encrypted | null.

failure_scenarios.title: Customer builds stop compiling after a minor upgrade when encrypting Json values typed JsonDocument
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer upgrades @cipherstash/stack within its semver range and has code like `const r = await client.encrypt(doc, { table, column: t.metadata }); r.data.c` where `doc: JsonDocument` (or a variable whose type admits null).
failure_scenarios.mechanism:
EncryptResult

adds `null` to the success type whenever P admits null (operations/encrypt.ts:41); EncryptionClient.encrypt now returns EncryptOperation> (client-v3.ts:196). The changeset declares this a `minor` bump and says such code must now null-check.
failure_scenarios.consequence: TypeScript compile errors in consumer projects (strictNullChecks) on a minor release; deploys blocked until code is updated. No runtime or data change: the value was already null at runtime, so the new type is more accurate.

existing_verification.description: typed-client-v3.test-d.ts asserts Encrypted | null for literal null and JsonDocument-typed plaintexts and plain Encrypted for non-null values (including explicit <Table, Col> type args).

missing_verification: No check that in-repo examples/docs snippets encrypting Json values still type-check (none found by grep, but docs code is not compiled).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Call out the type change prominently in release notes (it is in the changeset); a reviewer should confirm the team accepts a type-only breaking change in a minor release rather than a major.

failure_scenarios.title: Verbatim ...args forwarding changes native encryptQuery routing for an untyped or adapter caller
failure_scenarios.trigger: A JS or `as never` caller (stack-drizzle, stack-prisma, plain JS) calls encryptQuery with an unusual argument list, e.g. (termsArray, undefined) or (array, null).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Typed client now passes ...args through unchanged (client-v3.ts:529-533); native discriminates on `!args[1]` (index.ts:349-364), the same truthiness test previously applied to `opts`. On read, every argument shape routes as before; only the arity seen by the native method differs.
failure_scenarios.consequence: If routing differed, a scalar array plaintext could be treated as a batch (or vice versa), producing wrong query terms or a thrown error. No such divergence was found; listed so a reviewer can confirm equivalence.

evidence.claim: EncryptionClient.encrypt returns EncryptOperation> with P defaulting to the column plaintext type.

EncryptResult

= Encrypted | (null & P); EncryptOperation takes result type R defaulting to Encrypted.
Type tests assert Encrypted | null for a literal null and a JsonDocument-typed plaintext on a Json column.
Typed client's encryptQuery implementation forwards ...args unchanged to the native client.

Native encryptQuery routes to batch when !args[1] and args[0] is a term array, empty-array batch when !args[1], throws without options, else single EncryptQueryOperation — same branches as the base opts-based version.
encryptGroupPerTerm raises encryptionFailure when result.data === null.
The per-term fallback is used only when the client has no bulkEncrypt; the bulk path already rejected null envelopes.
toJsPlaintext is an identity type assertion; no runtime transformation of plaintext.
Unit tests check encrypt and encryptQuery forwarding, including that the batch form reaches the native method with exactly one argument.
A test covers rejection of a null envelope on the per-term fallback.
stack-drizzle calls encryptQuery through a structural view with never-typed operands (single and batch forms).
Changeset bumps @cipherstash/stack minor and states that code reading result.data after encrypting a possibly-null Json value must now null-check.
Encryption() constructs NativeEncryptionClient and always returns createEncryptionClient(...) — the native class is not handed to callers.
At base, native encryptModel was generic and returned EncryptModelOperation<EncryptedFromBuildableTable<T, Table>>; head drops this to Record<string, unknown>.
Shipped skill text updated to describe null Json encrypt results.
Integration test round-trips a JSON document with null array elements through bulkEncrypt (needs credentials; not run).
